isolation_detail: Partial isolation: this is a re-audit using the auditor first-round report and closure criteria. No claim of a blind first pass or final independent acceptance. No implementer chat or defense was supplied; v2 is the object under audit. No controlled unblinding occurred.

finding_statuses.reason: The initial lease must match a challenge-bound human-approved digest. This closes the direct self-issuance hole in principle. The named issuance edge is illegal (R1). Approved route facts and current policy comparison remain unspecified. The contract field list omits route/permission ceilings although the precedence rule requires them. Dependent invalidation uses an optional submitted list and accepts old records as named-unit-only; it does not define derivation from approved dependencies or fail-closed legacy handling.

The before-launch seam and live-checkout recapture are substantial corrections. The current repaired controller has stable per-attempt dispatch IDs and recovery. The proposed hook does not bind those IDs, immutable envelope, clone baseline, exact selected route or launch receipt to a host reservation. Optional-hook fail-closed activation, idempotence and concurrency are unspecified (R4). Permitted escalation membership does not satisfy the human escalation gate (R3).

The immutable semantic contract binds statements, check argv, thresholds, non-goals and evidence requirements. Its digest is human-approved. Result dispositions remain separate. A threshold change with unchanged IDs must invalidate verification and require reauthorization. Independent result provenance and scorecard edge cases remain obligations under A4/A8; this is not a claim that those implementations exist.

Cumulative unresolved snapshots, same-head evidence repair and reopened IDs address major errors. New disposition rules violate the architecture and cannot use the claimed downgrade path (R2). The last finding cannot disappear via an empty snapshot with the current reducer (R5). There is no report-verdict-to-host-verdict table, independently verified per-criterion mapping, or trusted launch/context provenance rule beyond asserted route/isolation fields.

Final closure, external effects, metadata, immutable evidence/policy/contract bindings and a compiled floor are now explicit. The independence table omits disputed validation. A packet binds a reviewer route, but not explicit reviewer launch/context provenance. Import must preserve the existing separate-context and distinct-worker checks. The detector does not state fail-closed behavior for unknown interface/path classification.

The inequality is fixed. Direct work, inner attempts, reroutes, crash accounting, unmetered refusal and the two-failure stop rule are stated. Stable HMA reservation/result identity, atomic shared counters, monotonic spending across renewal, time-of-launch authorization and exact route binding remain absent (R4). Merely citing section 17 does not reconcile the automatic escalation design (R3).

D3 explicitly includes verified closure/release work or requires an explicit acceptance reduction. PARTIAL is no longer offered as equivalent completion. D4 supplies the prior audit alternative: independently review preserved work plus Gate B fixes, authorize a commit, then start from a clean tree. Gate B must still freeze and independently review the later loop result before proceeding. D3/D4 are proposed human decisions, not approvals already received.

All seven minimum proofs now have a gate and candidate test names. This is useful design evidence, not code proof. The matrix still omits concrete command/owner/expected-refusal assignments and key controls: renewal/concurrent reservation/replay, report provenance/verdict and criterion credit, disputed validation, N2 nonrepository/mutating-command cases, and empty-final-findings clearing. A test name such as TestNoSecondStageProjection is not a check of all duplicate-state behavior.

The revised design explicitly binds the review to head/diff/worktree, and packet changes make it stale. Gate B is assigned the fix and TestReviewBoundToArtifact. Retain the original A-versus-B, dirty-byte and valid-A controls. Code remains unchanged and the reproduced defect remains open until Gate B.

The revised design explicitly requires a snapshot of tested Git content and comparison with the approval. It also requires HMA recapture rather than trusting loop green. This is a sufficient design obligation when read with the original N2 closure criterion. Gate B must still test nonrepositories, wrong checkouts, unapproved dirt and before/after mutation; v2 does not supply those tests.

findings.title: Hook bridge lacks a stable reservation and launch protocol
findings.diagnosis: The hook argv carries run/unit/lease/route but no controller run, stable attempt ID, dispatch_run_id, envelope digest, reservation result or receipt identity. It appends a dispatch before launch, but the design does not specify atomic check-and-reserve, exact dynamic route transmission, idempotent resume, consumed-attempt identity, concurrent callers, renewal accounting, or prevention of an HMA-bound controller job omitting the optional hook. These omissions prevent the stated one-actual-attempt/one-HMA-count guarantee. The repaired controller already has stable IDs that the bridge could reuse.
findings.expected: Each actual launch must consume one globally counted unit attempt under an atomic current authority check. Resume and duplicate callbacks must not double-count. Renewed leases must not reset spent unit authority.

fix.action: Define a typed versioned request/response using controller run ID plus dispatch_run_id as an idempotency key. Bind envelope/check definitions, actual selected route, live/clone baseline and lease/core/policy digests. Atomically check authority and reserve shared unit counters. Require an HMA reservation to launch; attach canonical receipt/result; never release ambiguous launches. Require the hook for HMA-bound jobs and define renewal, direct-work, timeout and cancellation behavior.
fix.why: Each actual launch must consume one globally counted unit attempt under an atomic current authority check. Resume and duplicate callbacks must not double-count. Renewed leases must not reset spent unit authority.

verification.method: Run duplicate callbacks, a crash after reservation before launch, a lost launch response, resume, two concurrent controllers with one attempt left, a route change, omission of hook and lease renewal after prior spending. Require at most the approved number of launches and exactly one count per observed launch; unknown launch stays reserved.
verification.expected: Each actual launch must consume one globally counted unit attempt under an atomic current authority check. Resume and duplicate callbacks must not double-count. Renewed leases must not reset spent unit authority.

fix.tradeoffs: A callback is the correct seam, but it must be a protocol rather than only a success exit code. Strictly reserve declared cost; it is not provider billing. OS protection against a hostile trusted host remains outside this audit.
fix.alternative: Initially serialize all work through one HMA controller with escalate_to=stop and prohibit renewal/concurrent nested jobs; still persist stable attempt IDs and receipts.

findings.closure_criterion: Run duplicate callbacks, a crash after reservation before launch, a lost launch response, resume, two concurrent controllers with one attempt left, a route change, omission of hook and lease renewal after prior spending. Require at most the approved number of launches and exactly one count per observed launch; unknown launch stays reserved.
findings.reproduction_or_attack: Two authorized controller jobs both observe one remaining attempt. Both hook processes pass the non-atomic remaining check, then append and launch. Or restart after HMA append but before durable controller acknowledgement: a second hook call consumes a second row for the same stable controller attempt. These are missing-protocol counterexamples, not demonstrated races in unimplemented code.

findings.title: Empty cumulative findings cannot clear the last resolved blocker
findings.diagnosis: V2 removes resolved findings from the cumulative snapshot. When the last finding resolves, the snapshot is empty. The current reducer updates only when len(Findings)>0, so it retains the old BLOCK. A valid independent repair therefore cannot finish closure through the proposed format. V2 notices replacement semantics but not the absent-versus-empty case.
findings.expected: An explicit authoritative empty snapshot must mean no unresolved findings. Omitted findings must mean no new snapshot. Resolution must retain its independent evidence trail.
